uni-health-x-physio.title: Physiotherapy (BPT) Study Companion
uni-health-x-physio.description: Anatomy for physio, exercise therapy, electrotherapy concepts and ortho, neuro and cardiorespiratory rehabilitation with assessment scenarios. It is a study companion and does not replace supervised training, clinical practice or a licence.

courses.title: Anatomy for Physiotherapy · Joints, Muscles & Range of Motion
courses.summary: Joint classification, planes and axes, muscle actions, goniometry and normal range of motion, as used in a BPT first-year assessment room.
outcomes: Describe movements in the correct plane and axis
Measure and record range of motion with a goniometer
Name prime movers for key joint actions
Compute torque about a joint

scenes.text: Meera, a BPT first-year, is asked to describe a patient's arm movement in one precise sentence.
She learns that every movement belongs to a plane and turns about an axis.

steps.title: Learning note
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or qualified professional. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Three planes, three axes
steps.body:
- **Sagittal plane** (divides left/right): flexion and extension, about a frontal (mediolateral) axis.
- **Frontal/coronal plane**: abduction and adduction, about a sagittal (anteroposterior) axis.
- **Transverse plane**: rotation, about a vertical (longitudinal) axis.

Example: bending the elbow is flexion in the sagittal plane.

steps.title: Joint types by structure and movement
steps.body: Synovial joints have a capsule, synovial fluid and articular cartilage. Types: **hinge** (elbow, interphalangeal; one axis), **pivot** (atlanto-axial), **ball-and-socket** (shoulder, hip; three axes), **ellipsoid** (wrist), **saddle** (first carpometacarpal), **plane/gliding** (intercarpal). Fibrous joints (skull sutures) and cartilaginous joints (pubic symphysis) allow little movement.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Calling abduction a sagittal movement: it is in the frontal plane.
- Mixing up the plane (a flat surface) with the axis (a line about which motion occurs).

scenes.text: Mr Rao, 58, has a stiff knee after two weeks in a splint.
Meera must place the goniometer correctly and record the reading.

steps.title: Goniometer technique
steps.body: Position the patient in the standard start position (0° neutral). Place the **fulcrum** over the joint axis, the **stationary arm** along the proximal segment and the **moving arm** along the distal segment. Move the joint passively or actively to end range and read the scale. Record active (AROM) and passive (PROM) values, e.g. *Knee flexion AROM 0–95°, PROM 0–105°*.

steps.title: Typical normal ranges (adults, approximate)
steps.body: Shoulder flexion 0–180°, shoulder abduction 0–180°, elbow flexion 0–150°, hip flexion 0–120°, knee flexion 0–135°, ankle dorsiflexion 0–20°, plantarflexion 0–50°. Values vary by age, sex and reference source; compare with the other side.

steps.title: End-feel
steps.body: Note the end-feel: bony (hard), capsular (firm), soft-tissue approximation (soft), or empty (pain stops movement before resistance). An empty end-feel needs caution.

scenes.text: A patient holds a 5 kg bucket with the elbow at 90° and the forearm horizontal.
How much turning effort does the elbow muscle need to resist?

steps.title: Torque
steps.body: Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the axis (N·m). A muscle must create a torque at least equal to the external load torque to hold a position. Load torque grows with distance, which is why holding a weight at arm's length is harder.

steps.title: Solved example
steps.body: Mass 5 kg, centre of mass 0.40 m from the elbow axis, g = 9.8 m/s². Weight = 5 × 9.8 = 49 N. Torque = 49 × 0.40 = **19.6 N·m**. If the biceps inserts 0.04 m from the axis (perpendicular), force ≈ 19.6 ÷ 0.04 = **490 N** (ignoring the forearm's own weight).

steps.title: Lever classes
steps.body: First class: fulcrum between effort and load (neck extension, nodding). Second class: load between fulcrum and effort (calf raise on toes). Third class: effort between fulcrum and load (biceps at the elbow) — most limb muscles, favouring speed and range over force.

steps.title: What a good record contains
steps.body: Patient identifiers, side, joint, start position, AROM and PROM in degrees, end-feel, pain (0–10), comparison with the other side, and a plain-language impression.

steps.title: Model entry
steps.body: *R knee, supine. AROM flexion 0–95°, PROM 0–105°, end-feel firm-capsular, pain 4/10 at end range. L knee 0–135°. Impression: restricted flexion of 40° vs normal side.*

steps.title: When to refer
steps.body: Locked joint, sudden swelling without injury, hot red joint, or neurological signs should be referred to a physician promptly.

courses.title: Exercise Therapy · Strength, Mobility & Progression
courses.summary: Principles of therapeutic exercise: manual muscle testing, contraction types, resistance progression and mobility techniques.
outcomes: Grade muscle strength on the Oxford (MRC) scale

scenes.text: Anil cannot lift his foot against gravity after a nerve injury.
The therapist grades power from 0 to 5.

steps.title: Learning note
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or qualified professional. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: The 0–5 scale
steps.body: **0** no contraction · **1** flicker of contraction, no movement · **2** full range with gravity eliminated · **3** full range against gravity · **4** full range against gravity and moderate resistance · **5** normal. Grades 4 may be subdivided (4−, 4, 4+).

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Anil moves his foot through full range in side-lying (gravity eliminated) but cannot lift against gravity in sitting. Grade = **2**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Testing with the patient in the wrong position.
- Allowing trick movements by other muscles.
- Using MMT where spasticity exists; use tone scales instead.

items.text: Cannot complete range in sitting but completes in side-lying

quiz.q: Full range against gravity but no added resistance is grade
quiz.why: That is the definition of grade 3.
Grade 1 is a palpable flicker of contraction without joint movement.
Spasticity interferes with isolated voluntary strength grading.

scenes.text: A patient wants to know why slow lowering of a weight can feel harder to control.
Muscles work while lengthening too.

steps.title: Types of contraction
steps.body: **Isometric**: muscle tension without change in length. **Concentric**: muscle shortens while producing force. **Eccentric**: muscle lengthens under load (lowering a weight). **Isokinetic**: constant speed controlled by a machine. Eccentric work can produce greater force and is used in tendon rehabilitation under supervision.

steps.title: %1RM load calculation
steps.body: 1RM (one-repetition maximum) estimated as 60 kg. A programme prescribes 70% 1RM. Load = 60 × 0.70 = **42 kg**. For 50%: 30 kg.

steps.title: DeLorme-style progression
steps.body: Progressive resistance uses sets at increasing fractions of 10RM (for example 50%, 75%, 100% of 10RM). Progress when the patient completes the target sets without pain or compensation.

steps.title: FITT-VP framework
steps.body: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type, Volume and Progression. For early rehab: 2–3 short sessions daily for mobility, strengthening 2–3 times per week with rest days between.

steps.title: Teach-back
steps.body: Ask the patient to demonstrate each exercise. Give a written or picture sheet, a pain rule (mild ache acceptable, sharp or lasting pain means stop) and a review date.

steps.title: Safety
steps.body: Stop and seek advice for chest pain, dizziness, new swelling, or numbness.

steps.title: Progression logic
steps.body: If the patient finishes 3×10 with good form and pain ≤ 3/10, increase load by about 5–10% or move to a harder variation.

steps.title: Calculation
steps.body: Current load 6 kg. Increase 10% → 6.6 kg, round to 6.5 kg or 7 kg depending on available weights.

steps.title: Documentation

courses.title: Electrotherapy Concepts · TENS, Ultrasound & Safety
courses.summary: Concepts behind common electro-physical agents, parameters, calculations and contraindications. Evidence for several modalities is mixed; always follow local protocols.
outcomes: Convert between frequency, period and duty cycle
Explain the gate-control rationale for TENS
Calculate ultrasound intensity
List contraindications and precautions

scenes.text: Dev sees a unit set to 100 Hz with 200 µs pulses.
He wants to know what that really means.

steps.title: Learning note
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or qualified professional. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Key parameters
steps.body: **Frequency** (Hz) = pulses per second. **Period** = 1 ÷ frequency. **Pulse duration** is the width of each pulse. **Intensity** is amplitude (mA). Duty cycle = pulse duration × frequency.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body: Confusing µs with ms: 1 ms = 1000 µs.

activity.prompt: Pulse of 250 µs at 80 Hz. Duty cycle as a percentage?

Duty cycle for 200 µs at 100 Hz is

scenes.text: Mrs Kapoor has persistent low back pain and wants drug-free options.
TENS is considered as an adjunct.

steps.title: Rationale
steps.body: Conventional TENS (high frequency, roughly 50–150 Hz, low intensity, comfortable tingling) is explained by gate-control theory: stimulating large-diameter afferents may inhibit nociceptive transmission at the spinal cord. Acupuncture-like TENS uses low frequency (about 2–10 Hz) with stronger contractions. Clinical evidence for chronic pain is mixed and effects vary between people.

steps.title: Contraindications and precautions
steps.body: Avoid with demand pacemakers (unless cleared by a cardiologist), over the carotid sinus, anterior neck, eyes, broken or infected skin, over a pregnant uterus, in areas of impaired sensation, and in unreliable patients. Caution in epilepsy with head placement.

steps.title: Set-up
steps.body: Clean skin, check sensation, place electrodes around the painful area, raise intensity to a strong but comfortable tingle, record parameters, test response after 20–30 minutes.

items.text: Muscle ache in the lower back, intact skin
Electrodes over the front of the neck

quiz.why: High-frequency, low-intensity TENS is the conventional mode.

scenes.text: The ultrasound output is 3 W through a head with effective radiating area 5 cm².
What intensity is delivered?

steps.title: Intensity
steps.body: Spatial average intensity (W/cm²) = power (W) ÷ effective radiating area (cm²). Pulsed mode reduces the time-averaged intensity: temporal average = SATA × duty cycle.

steps.title: Worked
steps.body: 3 W ÷ 5 cm² = **0.6 W/cm²**. With pulsed 20% duty cycle, the temporal average is 0.6 × 0.20 = **0.12 W/cm²**.

steps.title: Safety
steps.body: Keep the head moving, avoid over bone surfaces with high doses, over the eyes, gonads, malignancy, active infection, or areas of reduced sensation. Evidence for many uses is limited.

courses.title: Orthopaedic Rehabilitation · Sprains, Fractures & Post-op
courses.summary: Tissue healing, acute injury management and phased rehabilitation across common orthopaedic conditions, with assessment scenarios.
outcomes: Describe phases of soft-tissue healing
Apply a phased ankle sprain programme
Screen red flags and refer
Document a rehabilitation progression

scenes.text: Anita rolled her ankle two days ago.
Her recovery follows biological stages.

steps.title: Learning note
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or qualified professional. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Three overlapping phases
steps.body: **Inflammatory** (about first 3–5 days): swelling, warmth, pain. **Proliferative** (about days 4–21): new collagen, scar formation. **Remodelling** (about week 3 to many months): collagen organises along stress lines. Times are approximate and overlap.

steps.title: Loading matters
steps.body: Early, appropriately dosed movement tends to help organise tissue; complete rest for long periods is usually avoided unless a fracture or surgery requires protection.

steps.title: Red flags
steps.body: Inability to bear weight for four steps, bone tenderness at specific landmarks (Ottawa rules), severe deformity, numbness, or signs of a clot (calf swelling and pain) need prompt medical review.

statements.s: Inability to bear weight is a red flag

quiz.q: The phase with new collagen laid down is

scenes.text: Anita wants to return to badminton.
Let's work out what is really going on — step by step.

steps.title: Acute (days 0–3)
steps.body: Protect, optimal loading, ice for comfort, compression, elevation. Walk as pain allows, begin gentle ankle movements.

steps.title: Sub-acute (weeks 1–3)
steps.body: Restore range, calf and peroneal strengthening, balance work on a flat surface, then on foam.

steps.title: Return to sport (weeks 3–8+)
steps.body: Hop tests, agility drills, sport-specific movement. Criteria: full range, no swelling, strength within about 90% of the other side, confident balance.

options: After pain settles, on flat surface first
quiz.why: Progress from flat to unstable surfaces.
It may ease pain; it does not heal tissue.

steps.title: Goals
steps.body: Prevent complications (chest infection, clots, pressure sores, deconditioning), restore transfers, gait and strength, prevent falls.

steps.title: Precautions

steps.title: Escalate

courses.title: Neurological Rehabilitation · Stroke, Tone & Scales
courses.summary: Assessment of consciousness, tone and function and principles of task-oriented neurorehabilitation.
outcomes: Score and interpret the Glasgow Coma Scale
Grade tone with the Modified Ashworth Scale

scenes.text: A patient opens eyes to voice, is confused and localises pain.
Score the response.

steps.title: Learning note
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or qualified professional. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Components
steps.body: **Eye (1–4)**, **Verbal (1–5)**, **Motor (1–6)**. Total 3–15. Eyes: spontaneous 4, to voice 3, to pain 2, none 1. Verbal: oriented 5, confused 4, words 3, sounds 2, none 1. Motor: obeys 6, localises 5, withdraws 4, abnormal flexion 3, extension 2, none 1.

steps.title: Worked
steps.body: Eyes to voice (3) + confused (4) + localises (5) = **12**.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.body: A score of 8 or below generally signals severe impairment and potential airway risk; urgent medical care is needed.

lessons.title: Tone, spasticity and the Modified Ashworth Scale

steps.title: Scale
steps.body: 0 no increase in tone · 1 slight catch and release or minimal resistance at end range · 1+ slight catch followed by minimal resistance through less than half the range · 2 more marked increase through most of range but easy to move · 3 considerable increase, passive movement difficult · 4 rigid.

steps.title: Technique
steps.body: Move the limb passively at a consistent speed, comparing across visits and recording position.

steps.title: Not the same as weakness
steps.body: Spastic limbs can still be weak; tone and strength are separate findings.

steps.title: FAST
steps.body: **F**ace drooping, **A**rm weakness, **S**peech difficulty, **T**ime to call emergency services (112). Early hospital care can limit damage.

steps.title: Rehabilitation principles
steps.body: Task-specific, repetitive, goal-directed practice; intensity matters; use real tasks (sit-to-stand, reaching); early mobilisation when medically stable; family training; prevent shoulder pain by careful handling.

steps.title: Motivation
steps.body: Set patient-chosen goals; record progress with measures.

courses.title: Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy · Heart Rate, METs & Exercise Prescription
courses.summary: Exercise intensity, METs, breathing techniques and safe monitoring in cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation.
outcomes: Calculate target heart rate with the Karvonen method
Convert VO2 to METs

scenes.text: Mr Gupta, 40, wants a safe walking intensity.
Let's work out what is really going on — step by step.

steps.title: Learning note
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or qualified professional. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Formula
steps.body: HRmax ≈ 220 − age (an estimate with wide individual variation). Heart-rate reserve (HRR) = HRmax − resting HR. Target = resting HR + (% × HRR).

steps.title: Limits
steps.body: Beta-blockers and some conditions change heart-rate response; use RPE and clinician guidance.

activity.prompt: Age 50, resting HR 60. Target HR at 70% HRR (bpm)?

lessons.title: METs, RPE and the talk test

scenes.text: Sheela's oxygen uptake is 21 mL/kg/min.
Let's work out what is really going on — step by step.

steps.title: MET
steps.body: 1 MET ≈ 3.5 mL O2/kg/min at rest. METs = VO2 ÷ 3.5.

steps.title: Borg RPE (6–20)
steps.body: 6 no exertion, 11–13 light to somewhat hard, 15–16 hard. A moderate target for many cardiac rehab patients is about 11–14. **Talk test**: can speak in sentences = moderate; only words = vigorous.

steps.title: Common techniques
steps.body: **Diaphragmatic breathing**, **thoracic expansion exercises** (deep breath with a hold of about 3 seconds), **pursed-lip breathing** (breathe out slowly through pursed lips, useful in COPD), **active cycle of breathing technique**, supported cough with a pillow.

steps.title: Positioning
steps.body: Upright sitting or forward-lean sitting can ease breathlessness.

steps.title: Stop and escalate
steps.body: Chest pain, fainting, blue lips, or oxygen saturation falling below the target range need immediate medical help.

steps.title: Stop criteria
